scope: Theorem 10.2 (Box, sheet, and invariant-plane realizations) of the manuscript “Prefix Instructions and Incompressible Flows” (preprints/Prefix-Instructions-and-Incompressible-Flows-September-27-2026/manuscript.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 376 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8cd581420ec9967a), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 29. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every deterministic machine and finite input, and every fixed positive computable viscosity ν, each row of the following table has a finite effective prescribed force f = Fν[U]. The initial velocity is zero. The force and velocity are smooth with all mixed derivatives bounded; the velocity has bounded kinetic energy. On R3 their spatial supports lie in one compact set independent of time, allowed to depend on the finite instance. On the unit torus both fields have spatial mean zero. Their global solution is (u, p) = (U, 0). On the torus it is unique in the classical periodic class. For the Euclidean rows it is unique among smooth classical solutions with u ∈ CtH2 ∩ C1 t L2, p ∈ CtH1, and bounded u, ∇u on every finite time interval; pressure representatives differing by spatial constants have the same velocity conclusion. These are the specified cases of Lemma 2.2. The material trajectory from the listed fixed label a enters the listed fixed open set O if and only if the machine halts. In a torus row, the displayed interval is an arc of R/Z and O is that interval times T2. No force in this theorem is required to be solenoidal. The separator sine-plane row additionally permits an effective mean-zero solenoidal force with the same velocity and event. For arbitrary fixed real ν > 0, the same algebraic formulas and conclusions hold, with numerical evaluation relative to that parameter.
